example.name: refactor_dry_violation
example.scenario: Refactor duplicated validation logic in the monitor module
example.user_request: Refactor the monitor module to eliminate DRY violations in validation logic

step.approach: Review the monitor module for repeated validation patterns. Outcome: identify duplicate validation checks across multiple functions.
Create a validation trait or helper functions to eliminate duplication. Outcome: extracted validation functions that can be reused.
step.analysis: Ensure the extracted functions have clear, single responsibilities

step.approach: Replace duplicated code with calls to the extracted validation functions. Outcome: cleaner, DRY-compliant code.
Run cargo clippy, cargo fmt, and tests to ensure no regressions. Outcome: code compiles without warnings and all tests pass.

example.completion: The monitor module now has centralized validation logic, eliminating DRY violations. All validation checks use the extracted functions, improving maintainability.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Extract common logic into reusable functions to eliminate duplication
Ensure extracted functions have single, clear responsibilities
Always run clippy and tests after refactoring

example.name: apply_solid_principles
example.scenario: Apply SOLID principles to the crypto module
example.user_request: Refactor the crypto module to better follow SOLID principles

step.approach: Review the crypto module for SOLID violations. Outcome: identify modules/functions with multiple responsibilities.
Split modules/functions that have multiple responsibilities. Outcome: each module/function has one reason to change.
step.analysis: Ensure separation improves testability and maintainability

step.approach: Use traits to make the module extensible without modification. Outcome: new algorithms can be added without changing existing code.
Split large traits into smaller, focused interfaces. Outcome: clients only depend on methods they use.
Run cargo clippy, cargo fmt, and tests to ensure no regressions. Outcome: code compiles without warnings and all tests pass.

example.completion: The crypto module now follows SOLID principles: - Each module has a single responsibility - The module is open for extension, closed for modification - Traits are focused and segregated - Dependencies are properly inverted

key_takeaways.takeaway: Apply SOLID principles incrementally, validating after each change
Split large traits into smaller, focused interfaces

example.name: simplify_over_engineered_code
example.scenario: Simplify over-engineered code following KISS principle
example.user_request: Simplify the entropy calculation module - it's too complex

step.approach: Review the entropy module for unnecessary abstractions and complexity. Outcome: identify areas where simpler solutions exist.
Eliminate traits, structs, or functions that don't add value. Outcome: simpler, more direct implementation.
step.analysis: Ensure simplification doesn't lose necessary flexibility

step.approach: Break down complex functions into smaller, clearer ones. Outcome: more readable and maintainable code.
Run cargo clippy, cargo fmt, and tests to ensure no regressions. Outcome: code compiles without warnings and all tests pass.

example.completion: The entropy module is now simpler and more maintainable: - Unnecessary abstractions removed - Complex logic broken down - Code is easier to understand and modify

key_takeaways.takeaway: Prefer simple solutions over complex ones (KISS)
Remove abstractions that don't add value (LEAN)
Break down complex logic into smaller, clearer functions
